The present revision has been preferred under Section 15 of the Eavcuee Interest (Separation) Act,
1951 read with Section 151 CPC, by the petitioner i.e. Custodian of Evacuee Property, through its Assistant Settlement Commissioner-cum-Assistant Custodian General, E.P Cell, challenging the order dated 04.04.2019 and 02.05.2019 passed by the Ld. Competent Officer i.e. Ld. S.C.J-cum-RC (Central District), Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi whereby the Ld Competent Officer had returned a finding that Sh Jaswant Singh/his legal heirs are entitled for the issuance of sales certificate subject to furnishing indemnity bond to the extent of Rs 1 Lakh and further subject to filing an undertaking to jointly and severally pay any shortfall in auction sale MCA DJ No 77/19 Custodian of Evacuee Property & Anr Vs Jaswant Singh Page No 2/20 price on the basis of records which custodian department may trace in near future duly reserving the right of the parties to raise their respective grievances in appropriate forms with respect to the consequences of the acquisition proceedings.
2. Ld Competent Officer vide order dt 02.05.2019 had further transferred the right, title and interest of the custodian of Evacuee property in the suit property in favour of the LRs of the claimant by directing the execution of 5 sale deeds with further directions to Sub Registrar, Mehrauli to take the sale deed on record and to make necessary mutation/correction in the records in the names of legal heirs of Late Sh Jaswant Singh.

BRIEF FACTS 3. The Predecessor-interest of the respondents namely Late Sh. who had given the highest bid of Rs. 1,30,000/- and 10% of the bid amount was given in cash at the time of conclusion of the auction sale and as per the policy the balance payment of the auction money was allowed to be made by way of adjustment out of claim compensation.
4. After the confirmation of auction sale, Late Sh. Jaswant Singh had obtained No Objection Certificate of other displaced persons alongwith their consent letters for adjustment of claim compensation in the favour of Late Sh. Jaswant Singh and thus Late Sh. Jaswant Singh had applied for grant of MCA DJ No 77/19 Custodian of Evacuee Property & Anr Vs Jaswant Singh Page No 3/20 provisional possession of the land and same was granted by the concerned department to Late Sh.

5. Admittedly the land in question was thereafter acquired in the year 1963 on behalf of DDA for carrying out the Masjid Moth Residential Scheme and required notification under Section 4 was also issued under the then Land Acquisition Act i.e. Land Acquisition Act 1894 in the year 1957and 1959.
However the respondent was issued the provisional sale certificate and also the possession of land on the basis of auction having been conducted in the year-1956.

6. The sale certificate could not be issued to Sh. Jaswant Singh Narag due to the following reasons : -
I. Controversies with respect to inter se claims of the claimants/associates with respect to amount of adjustment to be made towards sale price of land in Village Maszid Moth purchased by Sh Jaswant Singh.

It is also a matter of record that some litigations were initiated by the other claimants namely Sh.
Ganga Ram, Sh. Sarabjit Singh and Sh. Jasjit Singh.

However, the same were decided by the competent Court and since the sale certificate was not granted by the petitioner herein, the LRs of Late Sh. Jaswant Singh approached the competent officer for grant of sale certificate.

It is also a matter of record that an amount of Rs 1,257.19 paise instead of 12,007 has been adjusted towards another property in Basai Darapur purchased by Sh Amir Chand and Brij Lal from the claim of Sh Ganga Ram MCA DJ No 77/19 Custodian of Evacuee Property & Anr Vs Jaswant Singh Page No 4/20 towards the cost of the land who was associated with Sh Jaswant Singh.

Aggrieved by the wrongful adjustment of an amount of Rs 1,257.99 instead of Rs 12,007/- Sh Jaswant Singh preferred an appeal before the authorized chief Settlement Commissioner which appeal was allowed vide order dt 01.06.1970 and the entire amount of Rs 12,007/- was directed to be adjusted towards the cost of the land actioned in favour of Sh Jaswant Singh.

It is further a matter of record that aggrieved by the order dt 01.06.1970 Sh Amir Chand and Brij lal preferred a revision petition u/s 33 of D P (C & R ) Act 1954 with the Central Govt. which revision petition was dismissed.
Against the dismissal of the aforesaid petition a Writ petition was preferred before the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi which too was dismissed in the year 1993.

Accordingly, a quietus was put to the issue of wrongful adjustment of the claim compensation qua Sh Ganga Ram and accordingly the entire amount to the extent of Rs 12,007/- was adjusted towards the cost of the land instead of Rs 1,257.99 and which position was explained to the competent officer who accordingly vide order dt 15.12.2003 directed that the amount of Rs 10,960/- be adjusted towards the sale price of land of village Maszid Moth in favour of Sh Jaswant Singh.

Similarly another application u/o 1 Rule 10 CPC was preferred by one Sh Sarabjit Singh for being impleaded as a party who also staked claim to the land in question purchased by Sh Jaswant Singh on the ground that he was the partner of the firm M/s Jaswant Singh & Associates.
The competent officer vide order dt 16.05.1986 directed the impleadment of Sh Sarabjit Singh as a necessary party.

Aggrieved by the same, a revision petition was preferred by Sh Brijener Singh Narang which revision petition MCA DJ No 77/19 Custodian of Evacuee Property & Anr Vs Jaswant Singh Page No 5/20 was dismissed vide order dt 13.02.1998 passed by the Ld Appellant Officer/ADJ, Delhi.

sentences.text:
9. The present revision petition challenges the order dated 04.04.2019 and 02.05.2019 primarily on the ground as follows :-
a. The direction to issue the sale certificate is illegal and without jurisdiction since the entire sale consideration/auction purchase price has not been paid. b. Since the land sold in auction to Sh. Jaswant Singh stands acquired hence the ownership of the said land is not with the Auction Purchaser from the date of its acquisition and also that the character of the land has changed in terms of monetary compensation in accordance with provisions of Land Acquisition Act, 1890.

c. Neither the custodian nor any non-evacuee co-sharer have ownership or any other right over the acquired land and only compensation can be claimed with respect to the acquired land as per the provisions of Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

d. That the Ld. Competent Officer has no jurisdiction to deal with the matter after the acquisition of the land and the right course of action was to direct the parties to the land to approach the Land Acquisition Collector under the provision of the Land Acquisition Act 1894 and filed their claims and moreover the right of the respondent had not become mature to claim the ownership of land as they failed to deposit the total auction purchase amount.

e. That the Ld. Competent Officer wrongly and illegally directed for filing Indemnity Bond towards the non-payment of remaining auction purchase MCA DJ No 77/19 Custodian of Evacuee Property & Anr Vs Jaswant Singh Page No 10/20 amount by the respondents as the Indemnity Bond cannot be substituted in place of actual payment of auction purchase amount and even the Ld.
Competent Officer failed to adjudicate the actual amount which was to be paid by the auction purchaser with interest for such a long period.

f. That the Ld. Competent Officer wrongly appreciated the provisions of Land Acquisition Act 1894 applicable to the land after its acquisition and the contentions raised by the Revision/petitioner has not been fairly and correctly appreciated by the Ld. Competent Officer and that it is pertinent to mention here that the Ld. Competent Officer failed to correctly appreciate the statutory provision.

g. That the Ld. Competent Officer also wrongly appreciated the provisions of Delhi Land (Restriction and Transfer) Act by observing it that it was made effective in 1972 whereas the document of the sale certificate which is a document of transfer is being issued after the commencement of the restriction act so it cannot be said the same is not applicable.

It is submitted by Ld Counsel for the revisionist that the competent officer has committed illegality in as much as directing the issuance of sale certificate pertaining to the land in question in favour of the legal heirs of Sh Jaswant Singh upon filing the indemnity and the undertaking to pay the shortfall in the auction sale price of the suit land in view of the issuance of the notifications u/s 4 of the Land Custodian Of Evacuee Property And Anr vs Jaswant Singh (Since Deceased) Through ... on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129371962/

Ld Competent officer vide order dt 04.04.2019 duly noted the fact that the auction sale of the land in question was carried out on 14.09.1956 whereby a privity of contract was established between Jaswant Singh and custodian department to whom the land was auctioned by the competent officers and as per the records of the custodian department Sh Jaswant Singh was entitled to the land in question.

It is not out of place to mention that during the pendency of the proceedings before the Ld Competent officer for nearly 22 years, the revisionist herein failed to bring on record the actual amount due against the respondent herein despite umpteen opportunities resulting into the passing of the order dt 04.04.2019.

In the light of the aforesaid position, this court does not find any error or infirmity in the order as passed by Ld Competent officer so far as the same pertains to grounds (a ) and ( e) for the reason that on one hand the revisionist is claiming outstanding amount and on the other hand not coming forward the exact details of the amount outstanding and payable by the respondent.

However, this court feels that since the outstanding MCA DJ No 77/19 Custodian of Evacuee Property & Anr Vs Jaswant Singh Page No 14/20 amount is clearly reflected in the order dt 15.12.2003 and also in the order dated15.01.2015, the Ld Competent officer ought to have settled the controversy on the basis of the admissions made on record with respect to the outstanding amount as claimed by the revisionist and recorded vide order dt 15.12.2003 despite the revisionist having failed to bring the exact amount till the date of passing of the order dt 04.04.2019.

16.With respect to the aforesaid grounds raised by the revisionist and as reproduced hereinabove in Para 14 at serial no (b), (c), (d), (f) & (g), which primarily relates to the aspects of the ownership of the land in view of the Acquisition of Land and the power to transfer the same by the Revisionist or to direct the parties to approach the competent authorities (LAC) for claiming compensation etc.
Ld Competent officer in as much as passing the order dt 04.04.2019 duly dealt with the aforesaid aspects.

The Learned Competent Officer, noted the applicability of the provisions of Delhi Lands (Restrictions on Transfer), Act which was promulgated and was made effective in the year 1972 who further observed that the same would not nullify the auction sale in question and who further held that the coming into operation of the Delhi Lands (Restrictions on Transfer), Act would not absolve the custodian department from issuing the sale certificate in favour of the auction purchaser.

Ld Competent officer rightly came to the decision MCA DJ No 77/19 Custodian of Evacuee Property &
Anr Vs Jaswant Singh Page No 16/20 that the subsequent events such as the issuance of notification u/s 4 of Land Acquisition Act in the year 1957 & 1959 and also of the acquisition of land in the year 1963 and subsequently the promulgation of Delhi Land Restriction & Transfer Act 1972 did not change the status of the parties and accordingly held that Sh Jaswant Singh/his legal heirs are entitled to the issuance of the sale certificate pertaining to the land in question given the fact that at no point of time the auction sale was sought to be avoided or cancelled by the Custodian department.

sentences.text: 9 17.The

Ld Competent officer in as much as passing the order dt 04.04.2019 confined the said order to the sole question i.e. as to whether the sale certificate could be issued in favour of Jaswant Singh in terms of the auction proceedings which took place in the year 1956 by specifically leaving the parties to bear the consequences of the issuance of the sale certificate, and the acquisition proceedings with respect to the land in question.

It was specifically stated in the aforesaid order that the parties were specifically left to take recourse to appropriate proceedings with respect to questions not decided by the aforesaid order dt 04.04.2019 i.e. questions other than the limited question of the issuance of the sale certificate.

The Ld Competent officer confined the operation of the said order to the issuance of the sale certificate conducted in the year 1956 vide which the respective obligations were sealed between the parties and which entitled Sh Jaswant Singh to the issuance of the sale certificate subject to the payment of the balance sale consideration.

18.Ld Competent officer rightly came to the decision that the subsequent events such as the issuance of notification u/s 4 of Land Acquisition Act in the year MCA DJ No 77/19 Custodian of Evacuee Property & Anr Vs Jaswant Singh Page No 17/20 1957 & 1959 and also of the acquisition of land in the year 1963 and subsequently the promulgation of Delhi Land Restriction & Transfer Act did not change the status of the parties and accordingly held that Sh Jaswant Singh/his legal heirs are entitled to the issuance of the sale certificate pertaining to the land in question given the fact that at no point of time the auction sale was sought to be avoided or cancelled by the Custodian department.
19.The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the matter of Saraswati Devi (dead) by LR vs Delhi Development Authority & Ors (AIR 2013 SC 1717) and dealing with the same portion of the land in question i.e. Maszid Moth, New Delhi in identical set of facts wherein also pursuant to the auction of the property, handing over of the provisional possession and acquisition thereof under the Land Acquisition Act 1984, sale certificate was issued in the year 1980.

The Hon'ble Apex court after elaborately dealing with the provisions of Rule 90 of the Displaced Persons (Compensation &
Rehabilitation Rules) 1955

held as follows:
32.

The legal position with regard to transfer of title in respect of the property forming part of the compensation pool put to public auction under Rule 90 of the 1955 Rules may be summarized thus : on approval of the highest bid by the Competent Authority, a binding contract for the sale of the property to the auction-purchaser comes into existence.
Once the payment of the full purchase price is made, title in the property would pass to an auction-purchaser.

In other words, on the payment of the full purchase price, the ownership in the property sold in public auction would stand transferred but the transfer formally becomes complete on issuance of the certificate of sale.

If in the sale certificate, any particular date is mentioned as provided in the proforma appended to Rule 90, such date mentioned in the sale certificate may be presumed to be the date on which the purchase has become effective but crucial date for transfer of ownership in the property in favour of auction-purchaser is the date when full purchase price has been paid by the auction-purchaser.

The Hon'ble Apex court in the aforesaid judgment rendered while repelling challenge to the Land Acquisition Proceedings upheld the validity of the issuance of the Sale Certificate in the year 1980 i.e post land acquisition which happened in the year 1962.

In the aforesaid Judgment the Hon'ble Apex Court clarified that the claim for compensation, refund or any other monetary claim would be considered and/or decided on its own merits in accordance with law and the order passed dismissing the appeal would have no bearing in relation to such claims.
21.In view of the authoritative pronouncement rendered by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India

, none of the grounds as raised by the revisionist in para Para 9 at serial no (b), (c), (d), (f) & (g) holds any ground and as adequately dealt with by the Ld Competent officer requires no interference.

As held by the Ld Competent officer in the order dt 04.04.2019 and in view of the clarification issued by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the matter of Saraswati Devi (dead) by LR vs Delhi Development Authority & Ors (AIR 2013 SC 1717), no fault can be found in the order dt 04.04.2019 whereby direction have been issued for issuance of the sale certificate pertaining to the suit land in question reserving the respective rights of the parties to address their grievances in appropriate forums on other aspects such as the claim for compensation, refund or any other monetary claim.

It is further a matter of record that aggrieved by the order dt 01.06.1970 Sh Amir Chand and Brij lal preferred a revision petition u/s 33 of D P (C & R ) Act 1954 with the Central Govt. which revision petition was dismissed.
